newsitem.title: PERU: Lima stocks keep nervous eye on Wall St, end off.
newsitem.headline: Lima stocks keep nervous eye on Wall St, end off.

text.p: Share prices on the Lima Stock Exchange closed weaker for the second consecutive session Wednesday as investors took profits and kept a nervous eye on equities volatility on Wall Street, brokers said.
"Investors are still taking profits after the strong advances the market experienced a few weeks ago," said Abaco analyst Marcial Aleman.
"They do it to play safe, beacuse the behavior of the New York exchange does not give enough confidence," he added.
The bolsa's General Index fell 0.26 percent to 1,659.55 points while the blue-chip Selective Index was off 0.05 percent to close at 2,381.98 points.
Turnover was 27.9 million soles ($10.5 million) on 1,430 trades. From a total of 82 stocks traded, 32 closed lower, 15 higher and the rest unchanged.
Trading was dominated by bellwether Telefonica del Peru, which accounted for 45.95 percent of the total amount traded. Telefonica "B" shares rose 1.62 percent to 6.02 soles on 1,812,046 shares.
Mining stocks closed mixed with Buenaventura off 2.55 percent at 22.90 soles on 19,524 shares, while Morococha rose 1.83 percent to 2.23 soles on 59,535 shares.
Brokers said mining companies, particularly those involved in zinc, had good prospects due to strong international prices and the market's short- and mid-term outlook was still good.
